write_source_value authors nil and p/T precedence, w error/mode validity, Formatter precedence, sharp-v GoStringer, then Error before Stringer for v/s/x/X/q. SourceFormatState authors source width/precision presence, flag queries including plusV/sharpV, raw byte/string writes with byte counts and nested Fprintf-style formatting through a separate printer. Partial callback writes are retained across panic recovery.

call_method wraps Format/GoString/Error/String plus their output formatting in native catch_unwind. A nested panic while formatting that panic resumes its original payload, with nil-receiver handling checked first.

Invalid UTF8 consumes one byte and uses RuneError; a terminal dot is a verb while an empty precision before another byte is zero.

parse_number preserves the pinned parsenum pre-digit 1e6 overflow check and its end-of-input consumption, including the accepted final digit above that bound. Bracket parsing consumes through a closing bracket or only the opening byte if absent, distinguishes syntactic presence from an out-of-range argument and retains reordered on malformed indexes.

Source argument consumption preserves initial/width/precision/final indexes, present invalid star operands, missing-star cursor retention, percent priority over bad-index/missing-operand outcomes, no-verb termination and suppression of trailing extra arguments after any explicit index.

SourcePrintfDirective.resolve_counts reads width then precision integer kinds once, rejects star magnitudes outside plus/minus 1e6, makes negative widths positive and sets minus/clears zero, and rejects negative precision. Ordered BadWidth/BadPrecision data precedes the verb result. Literal numbers retain the distinct parsenum range.

Value v/w directives move sharp/plus into sharpV/plusV state. Every in-range w occurrence is recorded before error-type validation, retaining repeated explicit positions and invalid/nil error operands for the existing canonical factory.

SourceFormat.scanned derives wrapping/reordered metadata directly from original format bytes and optional error operands. Existing Errorf consumes the resulting state through its unchanged canonical factory; rendered output is still supplied by the caller. The indexed compatibility bridge, source class selection and multiple/single unwrap distinction remain in place.
raw_format_scan_authoring.owner: Rust-only SourcePrintfPlan scans original format bytes into literal/directive spans, source flags, width/precision references, ordered star operands, verb outcomes and %w positions. SourceFormat.scanned consumes its wrapping metadata on the existing Errors.Errorf path. Count resolution classifies source integer kinds without user formatting methods. Existing canonical fmt error classes, per-value type views, CGP runtime context and derive-deftly ownership remain canonical. This pure printer control data adds no dynamic Go object layer, effects, tasks, provider registry or competing lifecycle manager.

SourcePanicHandlers supports nil/non-nil-empty/fixed backing slots, index/full-reslice operations and source-profile make/append growth. A range captures the header and length, then copies each current function slot separately without holding locks over user callbacks. Later-slot writes are visible; reassigned/grown headers do not redirect the captured range.

HandleSourceCrash copies additional-handler headers, adds logical call depth4, runs global handlers then additional handlers and reads ReallyCrash after those effects. SourceCrashPanic.repanic transfers the original owned recovered value via a private invocation-matched tag; nested callback boundaries forward a tag that belongs to an outer active invocation. The native reporter retains Observed a panic, panic/stacktrace and string-versus-panicGoValue field branches, with Rust Debug/recovery-stack output explicitly partial. SourcePanicHandlers retains nil/empty/fixed backing/offset/length/capacity views and reads each function value outside callback execution, preserving later-slot replacement and header-reassignment behavior. Callback lists are source function/interface data, not effect-provider selection. SourceCrashPanic uses an ephemeral per-invocation rethrow tag to transfer the original owned payload through its active callback boundary. WorkerQueue keeps its existing queue/count/task owners and runs crash handlers inside the wait-style iteration before the outer running-count defer and parent fatal guard. No additional task, registry or lifecycle manager is added.
